audit_findings.title: Post-year-end debt interest may be absent from the OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $125.0 million term loan; computed minimum annual pre-tax interest of $10.625 million at the 1.00% SOFR floor plus 7.50%, versus the $56.5 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Current interest expense must reduce forward equity-level OE; the June bridge also predates the August refinancing.
audit_findings.evidence: During the fiscal years ended December 28, 2025, December 29, 2024 and December 31, 2023, the Company recognized interest expense related to draws on the respective revolving lines of credit of $ 0 , $ 0 and $ 7 , respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The capital-structure mismatch is demonstrated, although the precise forward OE adjustment is not. FY2025 had no revolver interest, June 2026 debt included a $30.0 million revolver draw, and on August 4 the company replaced that borrowing with a $125.0 million term loan. Because the valuation is dated after that financing and retains interest expense within equity OE, omitting normalized interest could materially overstate value. Not deducting principal does not cure the missing interest cost.
audit_findings.action: Replace the historical interest run rate with the term loan's normalized after-tax interest, include ABL interest and fees if drawn, update the debt reconciliation through September 6, 2026, and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Recurring farm prepayments may be omitted from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed working-capital funding of approximately $15.0 million in 2024 and $30.0 million in 2025; revised 2026 forecast of $10.0 million to $15.0 million, equal to 18% to 27% of the $56.5 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash farm-recruitment payments reduce distributable OE when paid, while accounting expense enters COGS gradually through ROU-asset amortization.
audit_findings.evidence: We believe the impact to our working capital resulting from these upfront costs could range from $25.0 million to $35.0 million in fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The payments and their deferred accounting recognition are demonstrated; whether the OE series already captures the cash funding is unresolved. Even the revised 2026 range is large relative to the anchor, and the repeated 2024-2026 payments show that treating them solely as temporary working capital could materially overstate sustainable owner earnings.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile annual cash prepayments, ROU additions, amortization and contract maturities to each OE year; then rerun using the normalized recurring cash requirement net of any amortization already deducted.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may be unfunded by the DCF
audit_findings.magnitude: Revised filed next-12-month capex of $55.0 million to $80.0 million for Vital Crossroads plus $0.5 million to $1.5 million for accelerator farms, versus the $56.5 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Capacity investment required for forecast growth must reduce forecast OE or delay the growth attributed to that capacity.
audit_findings.evidence: We anticipate that we will incur approximately $120.0 million to $140.0 million in capital expenditures related to the new egg washing and packing facility with onsite cold storage in the next 12 months and will incur further expenditures in the years following.
audit_findings.explanation: The future spending is demonstrated, but the portion necessary for the DCF's 3% to 6% growth is unresolved. The revised minimum facility spending alone is approximately equal to one full year of anchor OE. Construction is now being halted pending demand alignment, which also undermines any assumption that capacity-supported growth begins immediately.
audit_findings.action: Map each scenario's volume growth to existing capacity and commissioning dates; explicitly fund all required facility and farm investment, delay associated growth until productive, and rerun the DCF.

audit_findings.title: The lease-cost run rate may not be embedded in FY2025 OE
audit_findings.magnitude: Warehouse-specific amount unquantified; aggregate operating and variable lease cost was $24.392 million in H1 2026 versus $11.910 million in H1 2025, a filed increase of $12.482 million
audit_findings.mechanism: A stabilized current-perimeter rent and service run rate must reduce forward OE if FY2025 contains only partial-year expense.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, we began using a new dedicated cold storage and fulfillment center less than one mile from Egg Central Station, operated and owned by our longtime cold storage provider, to improve operational efficiency.
audit_findings.explanation: Aggregate lease costs increased enough to be potentially material, but the filing does not isolate the dedicated warehouse from farm leases, supply-control payments and other facilities. The record therefore cannot establish the warehouse-specific adjustment or whether it would change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the warehouse commencement date and contract-level fixed rent, service and variable charges; separate supply-control and farm-contract costs, annualize the current facility perimeter, compare it with FY2025 expense, and rerun if the shortfall is material.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may capitalize an abnormal egg-supply shock
audit_findings.magnitude: H1 2026 net loss of $32.587 million and Adjusted EBITDA of negative $21.590 million versus the $56.5 million OE anchor; exact normalized OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary HPAI-supported demand and pricing can inflate the historical OE anchor and the earnings level carried through every DCF scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: In fiscal 2024 and continuing into fiscal 2025, HPAI-related disruptions in the supply of conventional eggs resulted at times in increased demand for premium egg products such as ours, which occasionally resulted in shortages of these eggs on shelves at our retail customers.
audit_findings.explanation: The temporary HPAI benefit was disclosed, and subsequent reversal is now demonstrated: H1 2026 gross profit fell $70.356 million, Q2 retail revenue declined, oversupply forced low-price breaker sales, and the company incurred losses. These results do not by themselves establish normalized OE, but they show that even the zero-growth case's perpetual preservation of the $56.5 million anchor is not a conservative normalization.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild normalized OE from retail volumes, premium spreads, input costs and margins under ordinary conventional-egg supply; exclude oversupply disposal costs only if demonstrably temporary, then reset the anchor and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Option-exercise tax windfalls may inflate the trend anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed share-based-payment tax benefits of $1.636 million in 2023, $10.236 million in 2024 and $3.456 million in 2025; the 2024 benefit equals 21% of reported 2024 OE of $49.2 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Discrete excess tax benefits increase GAAP net income and OE-derived trend inputs unless replaced with a sustainable cash tax rate.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in the income tax provision of $10.8 million, or 77%, was primarily driven by an increase in net income for the fiscal year ended December 28, 2025 compared to the fiscal year ended December 29, 2024 partially offset by a decrease in the tax benefit of non-qualified stock option exercises that occurred during the fiscal year ended December 28, 2025 compared to the fiscal year ended December 29, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The tax benefits are demonstrated, but whether the OE construction normalized them is unresolved. Their scale—especially in 2024, a heavily weighted trend year—is reasonably capable of lifting the $56.5 million anchor materially. Retaining SBC expense does not justify retaining nonrecurring exercise-related tax windfalls.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the tax provision and cash taxes for every OE year, remove discrete excess benefits attributable to award exercises without reversing SBC expense, apply a sustainable tax rate, recompute the trend anchor, and rerun the valuation.
